title: Ra and the Eye of Destruction
subtitle: The sun god tires of human rebellion — and sends his daughter to end it

beer.locator: Legend of the Destruction of Mankind, the beer plan; local text normalized characters 122463-123525
beer.excerpt: Now when the Majesty of Re, the King of the South and North, had come with the gods to look at the vessels of beer, and behold, the daylight had appeared after the slaughter of men and women by the goddess in their season as she sailed up the river, the Majesty of Ra said, "It is good, it is good, nevertheless I must protect men and women against her." And Ra, said, "Let them take up the vases and carry them to the place where the men and women were slaughtered by her." Then the Majesty of the King of the South and North in the three-fold beauty of the night caused to be poured out these vases of beer which make [men] to lie down (or, sleep), and the meadows of the Four Heavens[FN#61] were filled with beer (or, water) by reason of the Souls of the Majesty of this god. And it came to pass that when this goddess arrived at the dawn of day, she found these [Heavens] flooded [with beer], and she was pleased thereat; and she drank [of the beer and blood], and her heart rejoiced, and she became drunk, and she gave no further attention to men and women.

narrativeBlocks.title: Humans plot against the sun
narrativeBlocks.body: Ra, the ageing sun-king, hears that humanity is plotting rebellion against him. He convenes the gods: his verdict is that mankind must be punished — and the instrument will be his own Eye.

narrativeBlocks.title: The Eye becomes Sekhmet
narrativeBlocks.body: The Eye of Ra descends as Hathor — who transforms into Sekhmet, the lioness of war. She begins the slaughter and finds it to her taste: the destruction doesn't stop when the rebels are gone.

narrativeBlocks.title: A goddess who won't stop
narrativeBlocks.body: Sekhmet drinks blood until she is drunk on killing — the punishment has become a rampage no one can call off. Ra, who sent her, now has a bigger problem than the rebels.

narrativeBlocks.title: Seven thousand jars of red
narrativeBlocks.body: The solution is a trick: seven thousand jars of beer dyed red to look like blood are flooded across the fields. Sekhmet drinks them dry, falls asleep drunk, and wakes as gentle Hathor again.

narrativeBlocks.title: A warning about the instrument
narrativeBlocks.body: The story reads like a god-learning parable: the destructive power you unleash may not stop where you stop it. Egypt's flood festival reenacted the red-beer trick as a celebration.
